comment: The upstream revision every corpus rule came from. `tools/import-cxx.py --all --pin tests/corpus/PIN.json --git-repo <llvm> --check` must reproduce every .gisel file byte for byte. The commit is a plain upstream llvm-project commit: local patches in a worktree cannot change what was imported, so the corpus keeps the reviewed deviations below. `patches` lists the upstream PRs carried on top of `commit` (unmerged, or merged after `commit`); the official side of the A/B harness is built from a tree with them applied, which is why the corpus asks for the post-fix behaviour. When they land upstream, move `commit` past them and delete both the patches and the deviations. Policy: we track exactly this commit. There is no automatic sync with upstream main; moving the pin is an explicit migration (update commit, re-run `--all --check`, refresh the frozen artefacts, re-run ab/replay-frozen.py, and review the corpus diff).

official_base.comment: The official side of the A/B harness is frozen here. `files` is the sha256 of every file whose content can change a legalizer answer, taken from the exact tree the official library was built from. ab/check-pin.sh compares content, not ancestry: a tree passes only if all of these match. Changing any of them is a baseline change -- rebuild, re-run every direction of evidence, and update this map in the same commit. Do not edit the tree and leave the map behind.

informational.comment: Where the evidence was recorded. No gate reads these paths; they are here so a reader can tell which machine snapshot the numbers came from.

frozen.head: 700e551714cc
frozen.note: The corpus is imported from `import_commit`; the rule sources below are that commit plus the declared patches plus the three declared local deviations. The official side is frozen at `frozen.head`, which still carries the `core*` builders; the generated include does not use them and is checked against a pin-only header by gisel-ab/scripts/inc/check-pin-header.sh.

deviations.effect: numElements() spells out the release-build answer (0) for scalar element counts instead of asserting. The rule text is unchanged; an assertions build now answers the scalar queries a release build would. This is the one local change that can change an official answer.

memSizeInBytesNotPow2() reads the known minimum of a scalable TypeSize instead of the fatal implicit conversion. No target in this tree references that predicate, so it cannot change an official answer; it still has to be declared because the file's bytes differ from the pin.

Adds the core* builders that older generated includes called. Methods only, no data members, and no upstream constructor calls them, so the official library's answers are unchanged. The generated include no longer needs them: gisel emits public LegalizeRuleSet builders, and gisel-ab/scripts/inc/check-pin-header.sh compiles every artifact against a pin-only header. The deviation stays because the frozen baseline tree was built with it.

official_base.note: The corpus is imported from `import_commit`; the rule sources below are that commit plus the declared patches and the three declared local deviations.  `pin/make-base.sh` rebuilds the tree by applying `patches` and then the `deviations` patch files; `--verify` compares all twelve files in `files`.  The deviation patches are generated from the fork commits and are byte-checked against `patch_sha256`, so the official baseline is reconstructible from this manifest alone.
